question.prompt: A particle moves so that its speed for the second and subsequent miles varies inversely as the integral number of miles already traveled. For each subsequent mile the speed is constant. If the second mile is traversed in \(2\) hours, then the time, in hours, needed to traverse the \(n\)th mile is:

solutions.explanation:
For an integer \(n\ge 2\), the particle has already completed \(n-1\) miles when it begins the \(n\)th mile. This is the number used in the inverse-variation rule.

The second mile takes \(2\) hours, so its constant speed is \(\tfrac12\) mile per hour. Since only one whole mile has been completed before the second mile, the speed during the \(n\)th mile is
\[
v_n=\frac{1}{2(n-1)}
\]
miles per hour. Each mile has length \(1\), so time equals distance divided by speed:
\[
\frac{1}{v_n}=2(n-1)\text{ hours}.
\]
Thus the answer is \(\boxed{2(n-1)}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\). The rule applies from the second mile onward.
solutions.title: Compare speeds over equal distances
